title: How Far Back the Mean Kiosk Drawdown is Read on a Micro Market Agreement
content:
A thin quarter of kiosk trade widens the window over which a mean drawdown is taken on an Unattended Micro Market Program agreement, and how long the market has been open settles how far it widens. The mean is the total of the drawdowns posted in the window divided by the number of them, rounded to the nearest cent as it is taken, a figure falling exactly on the half-cent going to the nearest even cent.

## Schedule of windows

| Drawdowns posted over the three months to the day the discount is worked out | Months the market has been open | The mean is taken over |
| --- | --- | --- |
| fewer than 12 | 12 months or more | the twelve months to that day |
| fewer than 12 | fewer than 12 months | every drawdown ever posted against the agreement |
| 12 or more | any | no such widening is made |

## Notes to the schedule

The thin-quarter trip count is 12 drawdowns: a quarter carrying 11 drawdowns is below it, and a quarter carrying exactly 12 is not. The settled-market age is 12 months from the day the market was installed: a market open for exactly 12 months is at or beyond that age, and a market open for 11 months is less than it.

Where the quarter carries 12 drawdowns or more, neither of the first two lines is reached.

*Hypothetical.* An agreement posting 9 drawdowns in the quarter on a market open 14 months takes the mean over the twelve months to that day. The same agreement on a market open 9 months takes the mean over every drawdown ever posted against it. Posting 12 drawdowns in the quarter, neither line is reached, whatever the age of the market.
